item.title: Iran Won the Negotiation, Even Though It Lost the War
item.description: The full text of the framework agreement with Iran is now public, and it is lopsided. Iran gets most of what it wants, and it gets it up front—before negotiations on a final deal even start. The United States gets very little. Israel gets even less.

item.title: Strengthening Vaccine Production and Access to Routine Immunizations in Sub-Saharan Africa | The CommonHealth Live!
item.description: Katherine E. Bliss discusses the progress made by the African Vaccine Manufacturing Accelerator with Farrah Losper, Folake Olayinka, Shanelle Hall, and David Kinder.

item.title: Subsidies, Stockpiles, and Shortages
item.description: This installment of Charting the Middle East spotlights regional government responses to the Iran war’s widening impacts.

item.title: After the Supermajority: Ethiopia’s Trajectory Following the 2026 Election
item.description: Ethiopia's Prosperity Party secured a supermajority in the June 2026 elections. What does this mean for the country's domestic trajectory and its increasingly assertive role across the Horn of Africa?

item.title: Irregular Warfare: Winning the Cognitive Domain
item.description: The United States should intentionally leverage data for agentic AI models to catch up to adversaries and to win the cognitive domain.

item.title: G7 Critical Minerals Ambitions and Iran's Natural Resources
item.description: As G7 leaders discussed critical minerals coordination and strategies to de-risk supply chains, a U.S.-Iran deal opens the possibility for investment in Iran’s untapped copper as a new frontier for critical mineral investment.

item.title: Managing DRC’s Ebola Crisis
item.description: One month into a dangerous outbreak of the Bundibugyo Ebola virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, it is time to focus on the evolving big picture and a concrete way forward. There is reason to be hopeful that U.S. leadership can remain central and meaningful.

item.title: After Maduro: Human Trafficking and the Vulnerability of Venezuelan Migrants in Colombia
item.description: The fragile security situations in both Colombia and Venezuela create conditions that allow criminal and non-state armed groups to expand trafficking in persons.

item.title: Preventing Iran’s Military Reconstitution
item.description: Iran’s ability to reconstitute its military depends on its ability to import key materials and equipment. With the UAE’s role as Iran’s central reexport hub up in the air, policymakers have a narrow window to identify and disrupt new procurement routes as they take shape.

item.title: The War May Be Ending. What Did Epic Fury Cost?
item.description: Iran war costs are estimated to be between $34 billion and $42 billion. As neither the FY 2026 defense budget nor the FY 2027 budget request includes war costs, Congress faces a major battle over paying for the war.

item.title: Lebanon in the Shadow of the U.S.-Iran MOU: Risks and Opportunities
item.description: The diplomacy underway to end the U.S.-Israel-Iran war could deepen Lebanon's strategic setbacks—or it could provide a historic opportunity to advance key Lebanese interests and contribute to a more stable regional order.

item.title: States Weekly: June 24, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers June 24, 2026.

item.title: The Greenspan Lesson for the AI Race
item.description: Senior Fellow Karl Smith argues that Chair Greenspan’s legacy offers a lesson for the AI era: macroeconomic data is backward-looking. If U.S. institutions misread a new productivity shift, they risk higher rates, slower AI investment, and a weaker long-term tech position.

item.title: Anthropic and the Export Control Dilemma
item.description: In this week's column, Bill Reinsch discusses the use of export controls on Anthropic's latest models and examines the tradeoff between measures that may hinder industry competitiveness and the risk that, without such controls, advanced technologies could fall into the hands of adversaries.

item.title: AI Has a Memory Problem
item.description: As AI data centers consume a growing share of global memory supply, shortages of advanced memory chips are emerging as a critical constraint on AI deployment and industrial competitiveness. Policymakers must expand memory and packaging capacity to avoid future bottlenecks.

item.title: Trump's Smart Iran Exit
item.description: Jon Alterman argues in the Times of India that Trump was right to end the Iran war, not because the U.S. won, but because the conflict exposed the limits of military power, reshaped U.S.-Israel ties, and showed the value of diplomacy and partners like India.

item.title: Venezuela Suffered Its Worst Earthquake in Decades: What Comes Next?
item.description: Two powerful earthquakes, measuring 7.2 and 7.5 on the Richter scale, recently struck along the coast of Venezuela. The international response will be a major test of U.S. leadership and Washington's new relationship with Caracas.
